name: Closing Bell
statusNote: A small, complete single-file build — a low-stakes game, deliberately outside the design-gate discipline applied to the money-handling tools.
oneLiner: A day-trading arcade game: survive to the closing bell, bank the day, buy an edge. Not a real trading tool — no live data, no broker, purely a game.
stack: Single self-contained index.html (inline CSS + vanilla JS, no build step)

components.name: Topbar
components.desc: Bankroll, equity, day P&L, and the session clock.

components.name: Canvas chart
components.desc: Tick-driven price chart with a regime pill, news-tip overlay, and a telegraph indicator.

components.name: News tape
components.desc: Scrolling headline ticker; animation disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Overlays
components.desc: Title, end-of-day summary with an upgrade shop, margin-call game-over, pause.

components.name: Price generator
components.desc: Box-Muller Gaussian random walk drives the synthetic tape.

dataFlow: A synthetic Gaussian random-walk price path is drawn to the canvas each tick.
The player goes long, short, or flat (mouse or keyboard shortcuts); position and P&L update.
The clock hits 4:00 — the day-end overlay shows P&L, trades, and bankroll.
Optional shop spend, then the next day begins with difficulty and edge carried forward.
The game ends on a margin call with a final summary.
decisions: Fully self-contained — no network calls, no dependency on any other repo.
Styled independently of the house style: its own light blue/white equity-terminal palette.
prefers-reduced-motion respected even in a throwaway game.
